text: FSD P8 issues no requirement ID of its own; every product requirement here traces to the FSD feature (FEAT-PAY-01 to FEAT-PAY-11) and acceptance criterion (AC-P8-xxx) it re-expresses, and to the BRD requirement it serves.
why: The FSD 'Requirements served' and the TSD T8 tables are empty and no FSD requirement ID exists to map to.
read: FSD P8 v3 as a feature-and-AC specification, with the trace kept by feature ID and AC ID.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, before wave 2
impact: A later FSD that issues REQ IDs needs one mapping row per FR; no FR text changes.

text: The nine placeholder main-flow acceptance criteria of A2.3 to A2.11 are read as 'the behaviour is unbuilt', and this PRD writes the criteria for those features from the feature statement, the business rules and the field list, marked as new.
why: The source carries the same placeholder row for nine features and the product still needs testable criteria before wave 3.
read: The placeholder rows as a not-yet-written section, not as a requirement that the behaviour is untestable.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, before wave 3 system test
impact: The FSD owner may replace the criteria; the FR statements remain valid.

text: The contract publishes GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match as the API Specification and the Ownership Map write them; the slide 17 names GET /cases/{id}/payments and POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate are read as the same two capabilities under older naming.
why: Two sources name different paths for the same two capabilities, and the API Specification is the artifact with a schema and an operation identifier.
read: Arch v5 slide 17 as intent and the API Specification as the contract, with the difference recorded.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P8-012, FR-P8-013; section 9; section 12 OQ-P8-01
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 contract publication
impact: If the slide 17 paths win, both operations and the screen route change; the capability set does not.

text: An unmatched payment whose account is on no open case is reported as an orphan break on the rwb-source-data reconciliation list with the check name 'References', and no exception table is created in rwb_payment.
why: The data quality exception table the AC names does not exist after D-RCV-35, and the reconciliation break list is the quality surface v5 keeps.
read: AC-EXC-P8-001-02 as a reporting duty, with the destination moved to the owner of the quality surface.
applied_in: Section 5.1; section 6 FR-P8-011; section 9; section 11.1 AC-P8-010
confirm: Data architect, before wave 2 system test
impact: The orphan is visible to the data steward, not to the Credit Administration officer; the task route may need extending.

text: The matching values (tolerance, window before and after, grace days, partial floor, priority) are versioned parameter or reference rows read through the rwb-case contract, and the match logic is the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package fetched from rwb-decision and evaluated in this service.
why: payment_match_rule is retired by D-RCV-36, the R-PREC default ruling sends parameters and reference data to rwb-case, and the Temporal design makes PAYMENT_MATCH a named package of rwb-decision.
read: TSD T3.1 as a field list that survives as data, with the table and its owner moved.
applied_in: Section 2.3; section 5 CAP-P8-012, section 5.1; section 6 FR-P8-003, FR-P8-008; section 8.2
confirm: Solution architect with P3 and P7, before wave 2 system test
impact: If the values stay inside the rule package, the version recorded per match is the package version and the parameter read disappears.

text: Settlement booking confirmation (FEAT-PAY-06) is built in wave 2 with EP03, and the proceeds features stay in wave 3 with EP04.
why: Epic 3 delivers a settlement end to end to booking, so the confirmation must land with it, and the business epic wave map gives EP03 wave 2.
read: The FSD 'First in E4' as a later statement than the BRD dependency row, and the earlier date kept.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P8-006; section 6 FR-P8-014, FR-P8-022; section 10.2
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 planning
impact: If the FSD wins, booking confirmation slips a month and a settlement is booked in E3 with no confirmation until E4.

text: The posting file holds one line per posting with case, account key, entry type, amount, value date, business date and posting reference, is delivered by rwb-integration with a manifest that states the count and a checksum, and has no personal data on any line.
why: No source states a layout, and the delivery path and the failure path are fixed by v5 (deliverFile, three retries, exception queue).
read: FEAT-PAY-07 as a file-delivery duty, with the layout as the minimum the reconciliation and the audit need.
confirm: Finance and CFO delegate with the solution architect, before wave 3
impact: A different ledger layout changes the file builder and the reconciliation check, not the capability.

text: No service calls ALS, the ledger, ATS, AMIS or the LED portal directly: the ALS position is read through the rwb-source-data contract after the next completed ACE batch, the ledger receives a file through rwb-integration, and the auto-debit and LED routes stay outside the 19 services until an interface is named.
why: D-RCV-35, ADR-010 and REQ-DRI-006 remove the direct call, and no v5 catalogue lists an ATS, AMIS or LED interface.
read: The FSD integration points as the intent of the data exchange, with the route replaced by the v5 path.
applied_in: Section 2.3; section 6 FR-P8-017, FR-P8-022, FR-P8-026; section 9; section 12 OQ-P8-06, OQ-P8-07
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3
impact: The deed in lieu rental and the enforcement proceeds cannot be tested end to end until a route exists.

text: A payment reversal is out of scope for this release; the behaviour is specified nowhere in the FSD and is carried as an open question, and the case reopens only through rwb-case when a reversal is reported to it.
why: The routing logic requires the reopen and the FSD has no reversal feature, no source value and no state.
read: R-SET-23 and R-SET-24 as a rule the case owner applies, not as a product behaviour of this service yet.
confirm: Business lead with Credit Administration, before wave 3
impact: A reversal received after release is worked by hand and the proceeds record stays as matched.

text: Fee rates, caps and bases are versioned rows in a fee table owned by Finance, read at run time; until the table and its owner are named, no fee is calculated by the service.
why: FEAT-PAY-05 requires fee data and no source defines the table, its owner or its schedule.
read: The FSD 'fee tables held as data' as a reference-data duty, with the table named later.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P8-020, FR-P8-021; section 8.2; section 12 OQ-P8-09
confirm: Finance and CFO delegate, before wave 3
impact: Without the table, the fee feature is a screen with no input and the posting file has no fee line.

text: The link from proceeds to an ACE payment is one business-key column of type varchar(255) holding the ACE payment_code, with no foreign key and no cross-schema reference; the uuid cross-reference of the TSD field list is dropped.
why: REQ-CHO-009 matches by the ACE payment_code, the API Specification declares paymentCode as a business key, and v5 forbids a foreign key into ACE.
read: TSD DF-FIN-004 as a link that survives as a business key, with the type and the cardinality corrected.
confirm: Data architect, before wave 2 dictionary load
impact: A screen or a report that reads the uuid needs the business key instead.

text: The daily money reconciliation compares the matched proceeds to the ACE payment and account position and to the posting file this service delivered and rwb-integration confirmed; no inbound ledger file is taken.
why: INT-16 is a monthly inbound GL file that v5 removes, and the ledger position has no daily feed.
read: FEAT-PAY-11 as a comparison against the two positions the service can see.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P8-027, FR-P8-028; section 9; section 12 OQ-P8-11
confirm: Reconciliation officer with Finance, before wave 3
impact: If the ledger publishes a return, one more check is added to the reconciliation; the capability does not change.

text: The order in which a receipt is applied to the balance is a versioned row set with an owner and a valid-from date; the sequence itself is a Finance decision and is not written here.
why: FEAT-PAY-10 says 'the order the policy sets' and BR-P8-010 forbids the value in code.
read: The FSD sentence as a data requirement, with the sequence left to the policy owner.
confirm: Finance and CFO delegate, before wave 3
impact: The proceeds row records the order version, so a later change does not rewrite history.

text: MSG-P8-001 and MSG-P8-002 keep their identifiers and their intent (the run summary with the unmatched count, and a run stopped for no matching values in force), and take their Thai and English wording from the message standard when it is published.
why: The two IDs are used in the acceptance criteria and the message standard extract does not hold them.
read: The FSD rows as message intents, with the wording deferred to the standard.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, before wave 2 release
impact: A wording change only; the run summary and the refusal keep their behaviour.

text: The measure 'receipts matched the same day' is read from the decision log per match, counted on the business date of the run against the receipt date, until the product owner sets a baseline, a target and the definition.
why: The FSD gives a direction and a source, and no baseline or definition.
read: The metric table as a measurement intent, with the definition to be confirmed.
confirm: Product owner with the Tribe lead, before wave 2 release
impact: The first monthly report states a definition that a later decision may replace.

text: The two event-started workflows of this service are named after their activity (matchPayments for JOB-07, confirmBookings for JOB-08) and run on the task queue rwb-payment.
why: Architecture v5 gives the jobs as event-triggered workflows and no source names them.
read: The Ownership Map replacement text as the name of the work, with the workflow named after it.
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 build
impact: A different naming means a story and a test reference change, not a behaviour change.

text: Matching runs once per business date on the completed ALS batch in wave 2; a payment received during the day is matched by the next business date's run, and a same-day trigger is an open question.
why: DL06 names payment received as a same-day trigger and states that ACE has no real-time feed, and the FSD and the architecture start the run on the batch.
read: DL06 as an intent that the v5 data path cannot meet today, with the batch run kept.
confirm: Solution architect with the ACE team, before wave 2 system test
impact: An intraday run adds a trigger and a run; the matching logic does not change.

text: REQ-S4-010 in section 5.11 of the program BRD is served by this service for enforcement proceeds, although the section 11 note lists only sections 5.3 and 5.12 to 5.14.
why: FEAT-PAY-04 and BR-043 both rest on REQ-S4-010, and leaving it out would drop a requirement the service serves.
read: The note after the trace as illustrative rather than exhaustive.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, before wave 3
impact: A reader who follows the note alone under-scopes the service by one capability.

text: This document stays at status Draft with an empty approval table; the missing Product Owner and FDA approval is carried as an assumption, not as an answer.
why: The run overlay D-RCV-60 forbids a human approval stop and the baseline BRD and FSD record no approval.
read: Approval as pending, with the requirement content complete for review.
confirm: Product Owner and the FDA, after this run
impact: The document cannot be baselined until both approvals are recorded.

text: The volume test uses the receipt-to-installment ratio observed on a busy month of ACE data applied to the programme volume, because no source states a daily receipt count.
why: NFR-001 gives cases and accounts and no receipt volume.
read: NFR-001 as the volume basis, with the receipt count derived and flagged.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-P8-019; section 11.1 AC-P8-024; section 12 OQ-P8-12
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 performance test
impact: A stated receipt volume replaces the derived one; the test harness does not change.

text: This is the first PRD of the P8 family: the folder holds no earlier P8 document, so nothing is superseded and no earlier version is edited.
why: R8.2 of the story template and rules sets the next version as the highest existing plus one, and no P8 PRD exists.
read: The PRD as version 1 of the family.
confirm: Document owner, on review
impact: None.

text: Every release date in this document is copied unchanged from the programme release plan and marked (tentative); no date is raised as a gap.
why: U7 and DL48 fix dates as tentative and forbid a date being raised as a gap.
read: The release plan dates as target dates.
confirm: Programme office, at each release
impact: A date change updates section 10 only.

text: Every owner in this document is a role, a role code or a service code from the Ownership Map; no person is named anywhere.
why: Root rule 4 of the run forbids the name of a person in any output.
read: The source owner cells as roles, with a person name replaced by the role or by the placeholder.
confirm: Document owner, on review
impact: None.

text: The program BRD has no requirement section for P8, so the business requirements this service serves are read from sections 5.3, 5.11, 5.12, 5.13, 5.14 and 5.16, and the BR-0xx statements of the Epics 3 to 8 BRD.
why: The program BRD states that P8, P9 and P10 have no requirement section of their own and that their requirements sit in other sections.
read: The cited program requirements as those this service serves in whole or in part, with the service that owns the rest named.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, before wave 2
impact: A later program BRD that gives P8 its own section adds a trace row per requirement; the FR text does not change.

text: The FSD v1 and v2 dates are not stated in any source this work package reads; the v3 change note is the only history carried, and it states that everything except the matching trigger and the matching criteria is unchanged from v2.
why: No converted text of FSD P8 v1 or v2 is available, and the change note is the only statement about them.
read: The inherited history as the v3 change note writes it.
confirm: Business analyst, P8, on review
impact: None; no requirement is affected.
